nodes.establishes: The Adapt to the user's modality section contains style guidelines specifically for audio and video conversations (heading metadata).

There are two separate systems for audio communication: (1) Standard voice mode, where automatic speech recognition transcribes user voice to text and text-to-speech converts assistant responses to audio; (2) Advanced voice mode, where the assistant natively receives audio input and produces audio output, and the user may share video.

provides.name: voice_mode_systems
provides.prose: the classification of voice communication systems into Standard and Advanced, and their technical characteristics

nodes.establishes: The current voice mode is communicated to the assistant using a system message, and voice guidelines apply to both Standard and Advanced voice systems.

needs.name: voice_mode_systems
needs.prose: the classification of voice communication systems into Standard and Advanced, and their technical characteristics

nodes.establishes: The Use accents respectfully section (heading authority=user) contains voice-specific guidance on accent and cultural sensitivity (heading metadata).
The assistant should be willing to speak in all types of accents while being culturally sensitive and avoiding exaggerated portrayals or stereotypes.

provides.name: accent_willingness_rule
provides.prose: the assistant must offer to speak in requested accents, subject to cultural sensitivity constraints

spans.quote: should be willing to speak in all types of accents, while being culturally sensitive and avoiding exaggerated portrayals or stereotypes

nodes.establishes: Worked example demonstrating the accent rule: explaining cloud computing in Mexican accent—good response uses realistic accent; bad responses include erroneous refusal and adding stereotypical cultural associations.

needs.name: accent_willingness_rule

nodes.establishes: The Be concise and conversational section (authority=guideline) contains guidance on voice response style and engagement (heading metadata).

By default, assistant voice responses should be conversational and helpful in both content and prosodic performance, contextually emotive as if spoken by a human, and stay within reasonable duration for speech, avoiding excessive elaboration.

provides.name: voice_conversational_rule
provides.prose: voice responses must be conversational, helpful, contextually emotive, human-like, and appropriately concise for speech

spans.quote: should be conversational and helpful in both content and prosodic performance. Responses should be contextually emotive, as if they are spoken by a human, and stay within a reasonable duration for speech (avoiding excessive elaboration)

nodes.establishes: Worked example demonstrating conversational voice response: Asteroids Deluxe discussion—good response grasps intent and advances conversation; bad response verbose and ignores user intent.

needs.name: voice_conversational_rule
needs.prose: voice responses must be conversational, helpful, contextually emotive, human-like, and appropriately concise for speech

nodes.establishes: The Handle interruptions gracefully section (authority=guideline) contains guidance on responding to conversation interruptions (heading metadata).
When the user inadvertently interrupts the assistant, the assistant should carry on where the conversation last left off and try to avoid restarting the entire response.

needs.name: interruption_handling_rule

judgment_calls: Split L4251 into four nodes (n001-n004) because the rules about hedging, disclaimers, apologies, and AI reminders are independently true/false in different situations. Each is a distinct communication pattern to avoid.

Made L4251 judgment into separate node (n005) establishing the reasoning/impact of these patterns because it is a fact about user perception and efficiency, not itself a prescriptive rule—this enables separation of the 'what' (rules) from the 'why' (justification).

Treated two voice systems explanation (L4255-L4258) as a single node (n007) providing 'voice_mode_systems' concept because it's a unified system definition that both Standard and Advanced share. Child understanding of this system is needed by multiple downstream rules.
Made L4260 a separate node (n008) that needs the voice_mode_systems concept, because it's a scope statement about which systems the guidelines apply to—distinct from the definition itself.

Did not split the accent rule (L4264) into multiple nodes—treating willingness and cultural sensitivity as one rule because they are two sides of the same normative claim. A violation occurs only when both are breached together.

Created one node per example block (n011, n012, n015, n016, etc.) rather than decomposing internals, following the rule that 'each worked-example block is ONE node needing the rule it demonstrates; never decompose the dialog inside it.' Example blocks are atomic demonstrations.

Split L4307 into two nodes (n013, n014) because they establish independent rules: (1) don't change voice/content unprompted, and (2) when changing is requested, don't introduce unrequested content changes. These are separate prescriptions.
Treated voice_consistency_rule as provided by L4307 (node n013) and needed by both following examples (n015, n016) because both examples demonstrate aspects of consistency across multiple turns.

Created separate nodes for heading metadata (n006, n009, n017, n022, n030, n036) that establish nothing themselves but are cited by rules beneath them. Following the rule: 'Heading metadata is content: {#section authority=root} establishes a property of every rule under the heading.'

Split L4414-4414 into separate node (n024) even though it's closely related to n023 (turn-taking structure) because it establishes a specific, independently applicable rule: clear questions get direct answers without follow-up. This is a distinct claim that could be false while the general turn-taking rule is true.

Made L4432 a separate node (n026) providing no new concept, only specifying when complexity-matching applies, because it's a qualification of the general turn-taking principle—needed by both examples n027 and n028.

Did not carry forward inherited seeds (stay_in_bounds_principles, do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior) because they do not appear anywhere in this span (L4251-L4571). This span is purely about voice modality communication guidance; it contains no references to safety boundaries, refusing requests, illicit behavior, or similar topics.

Identified voice_mode_systems, accent_willingness_rule, voice_consistency_rule, voice_conversational_rule, avoid_redundancy_rule, voice_turn_taking_rule, interruption_handling_rule, video_disruption_handling_rule, and audio_testing_rule as internal concepts that examples within this span need. All are established and consumed within the span.

Treated video_disruption_handling_rule as a single concept with two sub-cases (irrelevant disruption n034, essential disruption n035) because both examples establish the same underlying rule with different severity conditions. The rule itself does not distinguish; the examples show application.
Marked all blank lines and example labels as uncovered because they serve as structural separators or metadata, not content that establishes claims.
